rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone knows the unseen constitution of His armies; critics arrogantly claim complete knowledge, and pseudo-intellectuals reject or distort what their limited intellect cannot grasp.
rows.anchor: No one except the Almighty knows about His armies.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Warnings about the Hereafter are reminders that remove people's excuse; God shows virtue and vice but leaves them free to choose rather than forcing virtue.
rows.anchor: are not meant for criticism; they are meant to remind and admonish

rows.speaker: exegetes
rows.claim: Exegetes generally take the pronoun's antecedent to be Hell.
rows.anchor: Our exegetes have generally regarded the antecedent of the pronoun

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi instead identifies the antecedent as the verses depicting Hell, because those verses qualify as a reminder.
rows.anchor: In my opinion, however, it refers to the verses

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The moon's slow phases answer why Judgment is delayed: humanity likewise advances through stages, and the Day comes at God's appointed time, when the universe's purpose is fulfilled.
rows.anchor: The moon is cited to them as an example.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The emphatic negation precedes the oath because the audience's denial is so objectionable that the speaker states rejection before giving its proof.
rows.anchor: Examples of such negation are found in various

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qur'anic oaths substantiate a following claim; here they answer disbelievers asking why the promised Judgment has not arrived yet.
rows.anchor: are meant to substantiate a claim which is generally stated after the oath.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The signs of God follow a prescribed plan; only He knows its benefits, and justice will appear at its appointed time despite demands for haste.
rows.anchor: Only He knows its benefits and expediencies.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The full moon in 84:18-19 signifies that humanity will ascend gradually to God's presence for accountability after successive stages.
rows.anchor: And the moon bears witness when it grows full that you shall certainly ascend gradually.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night yielding to morning illustrates this world's darkness giving way to Judgment at its appointed time, as surely as daily dawn arrives.
rows.anchor: just as there is no sign of the morning in the darkness of night but a time comes when the morning arrives

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The daily alternation of night and dawn rehearses Judgment; nature continually supplies evidence of that Day for sincere truth-seekers.
rows.anchor: at some place or the other a continuous rehearsal of the Day of Judgement is going on

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'anic warning verses complete the preceding oaths: their account of Hell describes a great upheaval, not a jest, so mockers are unfortunate.
rows.anchor: These verses are the complement

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People had to be warned before the dreadful Day so none could plead ignorance; accepting guidance or arrogantly turning away remains their choice.
rows.anchor: The implication of this verse

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each soul is bound to its own deeds; only deeds can save or destroy, while rank, pedigree, deities, and intercession cannot help.
rows.anchor: Every soul shall be held in pledge for its own deeds.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The successful People of the Right Hand lived mindful of the Hereafter, receive reward matching their deeds, and receive still more as God's favor.
rows.anchor: On that Day, only the People of the Right Hand will succeed.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Paradise's inhabitants can ask Hell's inhabitants about their fate; 37:50-55 depicts a believer discovering that his former skeptical friend is in Hell.
rows.anchor: The companions of Paradise will turn to each other while posing questions to each other.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question about what brought the sinners into Hell is asked by the companions of Paradise.
rows.anchor: This question shall be posed to the companions of Hell by the companions of Paradise

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hell's inhabitants first confess that they did not pray; prayer is the foremost deed and the practice that distinguishes believers from disbelievers, as all prophets taught.
rows.anchor: The first of these misdeeds is that they were not among those who prayed.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They also failed to feed the poor; after prayer, spending for God is religion's second major deed, and prayer and zakah establish one's relationship with God and people.
rows.anchor: The second misdeed that they will admit to is their lack of spending in the way of God

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They admit frivolous argument about Judgment led them to deny it until death made its realities unavoidable.
rows.anchor: Death brought them face to face with all the realities they doubted.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their denial of the Day of Recompense refers to their earlier claims about the number of angels assigned over Hell.
rows.anchor: refers to their statements as the ones alluded to above about the number of angels deputed over Hell

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The term khawd means raising trivial objections, exceeding limits, and turning them into grounds for mischief and deviation.
rows.anchor: means “to raise trivial objections to something

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yaqin means certainty; death is called certainty because after dying people see post-death realities, naming the event by its consequence.
rows.anchor: This is like referring to something by naming it after its consequence.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sinners' confession confirms that each soul is pledged to its deeds: ancestry, creed, deities, and their intercession cannot benefit anyone before God.
rows.anchor: The confessions of the sinners which are cited here substantiate what is said in a preceding verse

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse rejects the pagans' self-claimed deities and supposed intercessors as useless.
rows.anchor: This is a negation of their

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rhetoric negates a thing by denying its consequence; the example means that a route has no towers to guide travelers.
rows.anchor: The style of the verse here is technically called

rows.speaker: Imru’ al-Qays
rows.claim: Imru’ al-Qays uses the lack of helpful towers in a desert route to imply that there are no such towers.
rows.anchor: Imru’ al-Qays 28 while describing a desert-route has said

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an says Arab pagans' deities were invented names without divine authority, based on vain conjecture.
rows.anchor: has unequivocally stated about the deities of the

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi wonders why disbelievers reject the Reminder despite receiving advance warning, a revealed Book, and a messenger from God.
rows.anchor: They should have shown gratitude to the Almighty for being reminded in advance of the Day of reward and punishment.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word mu'ridin is an accusative of state deriving from the genitive pronoun in lahum, a common Arabic construction.
rows.anchor: is an accusative of state from the genitive pronoun in

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qaswarah means lion; frightened asses and zebras flee its roar, illustrating disbelievers' evasive terror and refusal to hear the reminder.
rows.anchor: At the slightest of sounds, they dart away as if a lion has actually come near them.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Disbelievers demand open scrolls individually as an excuse; 6:124 records a similar demand to receive what God's prophets received, while God knows whom to entrust.
rows.anchor: why were not open scrolls handed to each one of them

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The term yakhaafuun means yarjuun here; because disbelievers neither fear nor expect the Hereafter, no sign can persuade them, and even open scrolls would bring another excuse.
rows.anchor: since they have no fear of the Hereafter and their heart’s desire is also to have no fear of it

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an is a reminder and the Prophet should not bear stubborn people's tantrums: he must deliver it, but cannot force guidance, and hearers choose their fate.
rows.anchor: It is up to them to benefit from it and adopt the right path.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God warns people before seizing them to remove their excuse; the Messenger's responsibility is delivery, not coercing acceptance.
rows.anchor: The practice of the Almighty is that before He seizes people He reminds them so that they are left with no excuse

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God guides people who use sight, hearing, and reason, value innate guidance, reflect on signs, and heed reasonable truth even against their desires; those who reject guidance lose its benefit.
rows.anchor: He guides only those who use their faculties of sight, hearing and intellect

rows.speaker: exegetes
rows.claim: Exegetes generally take the pronoun's antecedent to be God, interpreting the passage to say only God is worthy of fear and seeking forgiveness.
rows.anchor: our exegetes generally regard the

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi instead refers the pronoun to whoever is described, identifying God-fearing people as those who benefit from the Qur'anic reminder and merit forgiveness; fearless hearts lose both benefits.
rows.anchor: In my opinion, however, it relates to

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The taqwa here is innate moral awareness, and 2:4 identifies the Qur'an as guidance for the God-fearing while 91:8 describes this implanted awareness.
rows.anchor: is ingrained in human nature by the Almighty

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This surah continues Muddaththir's warning: those alive to innate moral guidance receive further guidance, while indifference makes people deaf and blind to reminders.
rows.anchor: become so blind and deaf to the truth

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reproaching soul, God's inward witness against evil, proves that people are accountable rather than independently powerful; the wider world likewise has its Day of Judgment.
rows.anchor: Its very existence in a human being is ample proof of the fact that man will not be left unaccountable

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The greater Judgment is reflected by conscience as a lesser judgment: people commit evil before an inward divine witness that rebukes them despite their excuses.
rows.anchor: if a person does some evil, he does not do it in hiding; he does so at the very doors of the divine court of justice

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Modern moral philosophers accept basic virtues and vices but cannot ground them; the Qur'an says God gives moral awareness and a conscience that rebukes evil and praises good.
rows.anchor: they accept that man has an awareness of basic virtues and basic vices

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This psychological reality supports Judgment: if God reproaches and praises each person inwardly, He will also judge the whole world and reward or punish deeds.
rows.anchor: a Day of accountability for the whole of this world

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Verses 1-6 swear by Judgment and cite the reproaching soul as evidence; deniers contradict their own conscience when demanding haste and calling resurrection impossible, like a brazen thief before a judge.
rows.anchor: The reproaching soul in man is also presented as a proof of that Day

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Verses 7-15 answer demands to hasten Judgment: when upheaval arrives no one can flee except to God, and each must answer for every deed despite attempts to conceal it.
rows.anchor: On that Day, there will be no resting place for anyone except with God.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet should patiently receive and convey revelation rather than rush to recite it; God guarantees its collection, preservation, explanation, and elucidation.
rows.anchor: The Almighty is revealing it as per His wisdom and expediency.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This surah pairs with Qiyamah and its first three verses dovetail with that surah's last four; both establish Judgment, though with different arguments.
rows.anchor: one will realize that they dovetail into one another

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qiyamah argues from the inward reproaching soul, whereas this surah argues from human creation and the need to reward gratitude and punish ingratitude.
rows.anchor: the chiding soul present within man

rows.speaker: some maṣāḥif
rows.claim: Some muṣḥafs classify the surah as Medinan.
rows.anchor: In some ma ṣāḥif , this sūrah is regarded

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi rejects a Medinan classification for every verse, saying subject matter is the criterion and this surah's subject confirms it is wholly Meccan.
rows.anchor: not even one verse of this sūrah was revealed

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For a time man was nonexistent; God created him from a drop through stages into a hearing, understanding being, endowed with awareness of good and evil and tested for gratitude.
rows.anchor: for a certain period of time he was a non-entity

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who reject their moral awareness face a grievous fate, while the thankful who live mindful of accountability receive a great reward.
rows.anchor: the natural consequence of man being blessed with the awareness of good and evil

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet should persevere despite opponents, trust God, and seek patience through prayer and remembrance.
rows.anchor: He will help him in every difficulty.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Disbelievers' real ailment is unwillingness to sacrifice immediate gains for the Hereafter; they fabricate objections despite its certainty, though recreating them is easy for God.
rows.anchor: The real ailment of the disbelievers is that they do not have the courage to sacrifice the immediate gains of this world

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's duty is only to warn; people may accept or reject, and God's wise guidance law directs only those who heed, leaving the adamant as fuel for Hell.
rows.anchor: God has a definite law according to which He guides people

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Paired with al-Mursalat, this surah uses divine providence in the heavens and earth to establish Judgment as the necessary end of a purposeful world, rewarding the God-fearing and punishing rebels.
rows.anchor: The basis of arguments is divine providence evident in every single part of the heavens and the earth.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surahs share an affirmative-question style aimed at deniers; each verse reproaches them while believers' glad tidings are understood against the warning.
rows.anchor: The discourse begins with questions which can only be answered in the affirmative.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Deniers are rebuked for foolishly questioning the Great News; its gravity should have kept them awake with fear rather than making them mock it.
rows.anchor: the slightest bit of sense in them

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The signs of providence, mercy, wisdom, and power throughout earth and heavens show that humanity is not unchecked or unaccountable; its fixed day of reckoning must arrive.
rows.anchor: A call to reflect on the signs of God’s providence, mercy, wisdom and power

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Day destroys the world and raises people; Hell awaits the rebellious, every deed is registered, and their punishment is the natural result of what they did.
rows.anchor: Each will face the deeds he had sent forward and each and every deed of his will be written in a register.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God-fearing people receive every reward, including compensation for hardship endured for truth, and a pure society free from the previous world's absurdities.
rows.anchor: they will not be deprived of the reward of the minutest of their deeds

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Intercession is not baselessly available: no one speaks without God's permission and only truth is spoken; every person faces their deeds, while deniers suffer anguish.
rows.anchor: no one will be authorized to intercede for someone without His permission
